Hi Tom — great to hear you're moving this forward. Quick note on the DST mismatch: this year the EU moves their clocks one week earlier than the US, which creates a floating one-hour offset for about a week. For multi-region demos we typically either:
- run two short region-focused sessions (EMEA+US in one window, APAC in a second) or
- pick a single time that minimizes pain (late morning ET / late afternoon CET) and record with a live APAC Q&A in a separate slot.

I’ve copied Karthik (solutions) and Naomi (sales ops) to propose concrete windows. If you can share the preferred attendee list and any must-have time constraints for APAC, we’ll put together a clean calendar proposal and a timezone grid.

Also attaching a quick timezone matrix we use for these handoffs.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[g] grace.oconnor@redwood.com | m: +1 415 555 0198

Hi Tom — thanks for the context.

Short answer: because of the EU/US offset week we recommend one of the following options so you don’t have to juggle a tricky single time:

Option A — Two focused sessions (recommended)
  - EMEA + US: Wed, 5 Apr, 15:00 UTC (11:00 ET / 16:00 CET) — 45m walkthrough, ops Q&A for US/EMEA
  - APAC: Thu, 6 Apr, 01:00 UTC (11:00 AEST local for Sydney/Brisbane) — 30m demo + APAC-specific infra Q&A

Option B — Single session (compromise)
  - Thu, 6 Apr, 14:00 UTC (10:00 ET / 15:00 CET / 00:00 AEST) — we record main demo and run live APAC Q&A in the last 15 minutes; expect APAC participants to join slightly later/earlier than usual that week.

I’ve attached a visual calendar grid and a short MAP (mutual action plan) that maps attendees to the session they’d most benefit from. If you prefer, we can also run the APAC session at a later local time on Thu so it’s not overnight for your Singapore team.

Please confirm which option you prefer and any required attendees (e.g., security/compliance) so we can send official invites.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
